claims.text: Applying a strong static magnetic field during solidification can increase the coercive field of a magnetic high-entropy alloy.
A strong static magnetic field during solidification can influence the alloy microstructure.
A strong static magnetic field during solidification can influence atomic-level structure and defects.
The intervention is applied while the magnetic high-entropy alloy is molten or semi-solid.
Static magnetic-field intensities up to 5 T are relevant solidification conditions.
Magnetic-field-assisted solidification changes phase species and phase volume fractions.
Magnetic-field-assisted solidification changes vacancy and dislocation densities.
The resulting microstructural and defect changes alter the magnetic-domain structure.
Changes in magnetic-domain structure caused by the intervention produce an increase in coercive field.
The field-solidified alloy will have a higher coercive field than the same alloy solidified without a magnetic field.
The coercivity effect will be significant at field intensities that produce noticeable microstructural and defect changes.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase and the optimal field intensity may depend on alloy composition and solidification conditions.
A matched comparison of samples solidified with and without a static magnetic field, followed by coercive-field measurement, can test the hypothesis.
Failure of the field-treated sample to show a significantly higher coercive field than the no-field control would falsify the hypothesis.
